summary: The candidate is correct. The selector atoms have weights r_z/2 bounded by their fiber depths, so atomic halfspace domination and both rank factors apply exactly. In the affine case, the lattice centerpoint and every barycentric representation provide a valid complete-core certificate of total mass 2Omega. Finally, on the 1/5 affine tube, nesting puts s(z) in the quarter-mass metronoid, hence gives depth at least r_z/4; the residual-selector inequality then yields sum r_z <= 4H(C)W. Zero-load edges, lower-dimensional affine hulls, singleton/rank-zero supports, boundary halfspaces, and all stated quantifiers are handled.
